$comment: Construction-share classifier rules for roadmap 5.2.1.
The denominator is every py-spy raw stack containing a frame matching
consume_frames. The numerator is those stacks that also contain a frame
resolved by one of construction_rules, counted once per stack.
dataclasses.dataclass generates __init__ via exec(), so a generated
constructor's frame has location '<string>' and carries no class
identity in a py-spy capture -- every generated constructor in the
process renders the same way. Each rule therefore pairs its frame
pattern with the callers that reach it. The frame pattern for a
generated constructor deliberately leaves 'line' unset: the line number
shifts whenever the class gains a field, and pinning it would turn a
harmless field addition into a silently unresolved frame.
Callers name every production site that reaches the constructor, not
only the immediate one, so initialization moved into a helper still
resolves. Verified against the 5.2.1 baseline tree; re-verify with
grep before trusting an edit to the production call paths.
RE-BASELINED for EP-M2 (the hoist itself). What changed and why:
1. There is now ONE construction rule, not two. Before the hoist the
two rules split by caller: the per-line ExecEvent came through `emit`
and the per-line _EventDetails came through the `_event_details`
helper. The hoist deletes that helper, so the rule naming it can
never match again, and a rule whose callers still run while it matches
nothing is exactly what _drifted_rules reports -- the whole run would
exit 2 as inconclusive_drifted_rules.
The replacement cannot simply be a differently-named second rule.
_matching_rule gives a generated-constructor frame to the rule whose
nearest matching caller is closest to it, so two rules over the frame
`__init__ (<string>)` do not partition the samples by caller set: the
one with the nearer caller takes every frame both could claim. A rule
that therefore matches nothing while its callers still run is exactly
what _drifted_rules reports, and the run exits 2.
This was measured, not reasoned: a two-rule split over a stack of the
post-hoist shape (`emit_line` at _line_callbacks.py, then at
_pipeline_types.py, then `__init__`) gives the nearer-caller rule all
100 samples and reports the other as drifted with 100 caller samples.
The pre-hoist split only worked because `_event_details` was genuinely
the nearest caller for its own 4230 frames; the hoist removes it, and
with it any per-frame population the second rule could still win.
Merging them is also the stricter option, since N is meant to count
every constructor the emission path performs, whether or not it is per
line.
2. The surviving rule's callers were corrected. `_LineEventEmitter` and
`_emit_line_event` named nothing that exists in the production tree
and were dropped. `emit_line` at `cuprum/_pipeline_types.py` was also
dropped, and the reason is worth recording: it was never where the
hoist put the emitter. The emitter landed as a `_LineEventEmitter`
method in `cuprum/_line_callbacks.py`, where py-spy renders it with a
bare name as `emit_line`. Measured against the control capture: zero
frames carry `_pipeline_types.py` in an `emit_line` frame, and 111
carry `_line_callbacks.py`. Re-running the classifier with the entry
removed leaves every field of the control result identical, so the
entry was inert on the capture as well as absent from the tree.
`emit_line` at `cuprum/_line_callbacks.py` is the entry that does the
work, and it is the right one for a durable reason: the hoisted
construction happens in that method, and the un-hoisted construction
happened in the composed `emit_line` closure in the same file. One
entry therefore counts the per-line construction whether the hoist is
in place or has been reverted, instead of the measurement silently
scoring zero constructed events as absent work.
py-spy renders these frames with bare function names and a file
location -- `emit_line (cuprum/_line_callbacks.py:132)`, never
`_LineEventEmitter.emit_line`. Caller patterns must match that
rendering, and the line number in any example is illustrative only:
generated-constructor frames deliberately omit it because it shifts,
and the same caution applies to a handwritten frame.
The hoist's success is measured as: the per-line construction still
matches through `emit_line`, and its share falls. That no _EventDetails is
constructed per line is not provable from a capture at all -- the frame is
indistinguishable from every other generated constructor -- so it is
asserted directly by the tests that patch the constructor. See the
execplan's EP-M2 entry.

construction_rules.name: ExecEvent.__init__ reachable from the event-emission path
